title: Recognizing Shared Cyrillic Consonants: М, Т, К, О, А
primaryPurpose: Introduce printed capital and lowercase letterforms for shared Cyrillic consonants and cardinal anchor vowels.
communicativeOutcome: Visually identify and match Cyrillic letters М, Т, К, О, and А against identical Latin and international glyphs.
readingObjective: Recognize isolated uppercase and lowercase letterforms М, Т, К, О, А across standard serif and sans-serif fonts.
writingObjective: Transcribe uppercase and lowercase glyphs М, Т, К, О, А accurately into ruled line guides.
pragmaticTarget: Recognizing formal written educational signage and instructional symbols.
audioPurpose: Authentic articulation of isolated Cyrillic consonant phonemes without trailing neutral schwa.
successCriteria: Select correct Cyrillic letter from a distracter set of 4 letters consistently and accurately.
Pair uppercase and lowercase variants (М-м, Т-т, К-к, О-о, А-а) correctly.
masteryEvidence: Discriminates correctly between visual false friends such as Latin T vs Cyrillic Т.
Accurately transcribes 5 isolated characters on paper or digital canvas.

title: Navigating Cyrillic False Friends: В, Н, Р, С, Х
primaryPurpose: Differentiate letters that look identical to Latin graphemes but represent distinct Slavic/Mongolian phonemes.
communicativeOutcome: Distinguish and decode misleading letterforms В (/w/~/v/), Н (/n/), Р (/r/), С (/s/), Х (/x/) without phonetic Latin interference.
readingObjective: Read short international loan words (спорт, такси, парк) distinguishing Cyrillic P (/r/) and H (/n/).
listeningObjective: Discriminate sound values of false friends when paired with audio models of native phonemes.
writingObjective: Transcribe 3-5 simple international loan words without substituting Latin phoneme mappings.
pragmaticTarget: Interpreting urban signage featuring global loanwords.
reviewReason: Anchor newly learned false-friend letters into previously mastered shared consonant templates.
audioPurpose: Native pronunciation of initial fricatives and rolled alveolar trill Р (/r/).
successCriteria: Correctly classify В, Н, Р, С, Х by phonetic value rather than Latin value in 10 test items.
Accurately read aloud short loan words containing false friend letters.
masteryEvidence: Reads 'спорт' as /spɔrət/ rather than mistaking 'р' for /p/.
Identifies Cyrillic 'H' as alveolar nasal /n/ in initial and medial positions.

title: Blending Consonants and Vowels into Simple Syllables (CV and CVC)
primaryPurpose: Train the blending of shared consonants with cardinal vowels А and О into transparent open and closed syllables.
communicativeOutcome: Pronounce and decode basic monosyllabic and disyllabic letter strings with accurate phonemic boundaries.
readingObjective: Decode written open (ма, та, са, ха) and closed (ном, сор, тал) monosyllables in printed type.
listeningObjective: Match spoken monosyllables against corresponding written Cyrillic syllable cards.
writingObjective: Write dictated monosyllables and disyllables without omitted vowel characters.
spokenProductionObjective: Articulate open syllables with clear vowel release and non-aspirated voiceless stops.
pragmaticTarget: Responding to teacher phonics prompts in language training contexts.
reviewReason: Integrate shared consonants and false friends into active syllable decoding.
audioPurpose: Phonetically pure syllable audio without synthetic formant warping.
successCriteria: Correctly blend and read 8 out of 8 CV/CVC syllables.
Spell dictated monosyllabic strings accurately and reliably orthographic fidelity.
masteryEvidence: Distinguishes spoken 'сон' vs 'сан' and selects correct written representation.
Vocalizes non-aspirated stops without English-style aspiration burst.

title: Decoding Real-World Signs and Global Cognates
primaryPurpose: Apply learned consonants and anchor vowels to decipher authentic public signs, logos, and international cognates.
communicativeOutcome: Read and comprehend high-frequency urban signs (КИНО, ТАКСИ, БАНК, КАССА, АПТЕК) in public environments.
readingObjective: Scan and decode 5 authentic storefront signs and identify the corresponding service or location.
listeningObjective: Identify spoken place names when matching them with written street signs.
writingObjective: Transcribe 3 city facility names from signage into personal notebook.
spokenProductionObjective: Read storefront titles aloud with appropriate word-level stress.
pragmaticTarget: Navigating municipal transit hubs and commercial facilities.
reviewReason: Cumulative capstone application for Unit 1 script decoding.
audioPurpose: Authentic urban audio models of store names and public announcements.
successCriteria: Correctly match 5 authentic sign images with their English functional descriptions.
Accurately decode multi-syllable cognates with correct stress placement on the initial syllable.
masteryEvidence: Identifies 'КИНО' as cinema and 'АПТЕК' as pharmacy without hesitation.
Zero Latin-letter phoneme interference when reading words with 'P' and 'C'.

title: Identifying Distinctive Mongolian Letters Ө and Ү
primaryPurpose: Introduce the visual letterforms and historical background of the two unique Mongolian Cyrillic characters Ө and Ү.
communicativeOutcome: Recognize Ө and Ү in isolation and within authentic words without confusing them with standard О or У.
readingObjective: Distinguish between О vs Ө and У vs Ү in identical typographic environments.
writingObjective: Draw the crossbar for capital and lowercase Ө-ө and the straight stem of Ү-ү accurately.
pragmaticTarget: Correctly reading print and digital Mongolian texts without grapheme confusion.
reviewReason: Contrast new Mongolian letters Ө/Ү against previously mastered basic vowels О/У.
audioPurpose: Phonetic articulation of rounded front vowels [ɵ] and [u].
successCriteria: Sort 12 mixed words into groups containing О, Ө, У, and Ү consistently and accurately.
Accurately write uppercase and lowercase forms on ruled guidelines.
masteryEvidence: Instantly identifies Ө as distinct from О and Russian Э.
Correctly distinguishes Ү from Latin Y and Cyrillic У.

title: Auditory Discrimination: О vs Ө and У vs Ү
primaryPurpose: Train the ear to differentiate the open mid-rounded back vowel /ɔ/ from the front-rounded /ɵ/, and /ʊ/ from /u/.
communicativeOutcome: Accurately discern minimal pairs such as ор (bed/place) vs өр (debt), and ус (water) vs үс (hair).
readingObjective: Match spoken minimal pair audio recordings with the corresponding written word card.
listeningObjective: Identify whether the played vowel sound belongs to the back series (О/У) or front series (Ө/Ү).
writingObjective: Write the correct vowel letter upon hearing isolated minimal pair words.
spokenProductionObjective: Produce the lip rounding and tongue retraction necessary for distinct Ө and Ү sounds.
pragmaticTarget: Avoiding meaning confusion in basic domestic vocabulary.
reviewReason: Connect visual graphemes Ө/Ү to acoustic phonetic boundaries.
audioPurpose: Pristine acoustic contrast between Khalkha phonemes /ɔ/, /ɵ/, /ʊ/, /u/.
successCriteria: Score at least 9/10 on an auditory two-alternative forced-choice minimal pair quiz.
Articulate distinct vowel qualities without merging front and back vowels.
masteryEvidence: Selects 'өр' when hearing [ɵr] and 'ор' when hearing [ɔr].
Correctly detects [u] in 'үнэ' vs [ʊ] in 'унш'.

title: Reading High-Frequency Words with Ө and Ү: өдөр, өвөл, үнэн, сүү
primaryPurpose: Introduce essential daily vocabulary containing Ө and Ү across common domestic and temporal contexts.
communicativeOutcome: Read and recognize essential everyday words (өдөр 'day', өвөл 'winter', үнэн 'true', сүү 'milk') in print.
readingObjective: Read disyllabic words containing Ө and Ү in environmental food labels and calendar entries.
listeningObjective: Recognize spoken core items (сүү, өдөр) in grocery and daily life contexts.
writingObjective: Type or write 4 core words containing Ө and Ү from memory.
spokenProductionObjective: Pronounce 'өдөр' and 'сүү' with clear initial stress and proper vowel quality.
pragmaticTarget: Identifying staple dairy products and basic temporal units.
reviewReason: Consolidate phonology through practical lexical items.
audioPurpose: Authentic lexical pronunciation with natural Khalkha word stress.
successCriteria: Read 6 printed grocery and daily items accurately with correct vowel values.
Match words to pictorial representations (milk, sun/day, winter) without error.
masteryEvidence: Reads 'сүү' as [su:] with front rounded high vowel rather than back [sʊ:].
Accurately transcribes 'өдөр' without omitting vowel characters.

title: Decoding Mongolian Geographic and Cultural Names: Өвөрхангай, Сүхбаатар
primaryPurpose: Decode prominent Mongolian administrative regions, provinces (аймаг), and landmarks featuring Ө and Ү.
communicativeOutcome: Read and pronounce major Mongolian place names, square names, and street signs containing Ө and Ү.
readingObjective: Read authentic map labels, transit destination displays, and public squares (Сүхбаатар, Өвөрхангай, Төв).
listeningObjective: Identify destination names broadcast on bus transit voice announcements.
writingObjective: Write the names of two major provinces containing Ө or Ү correctly on an outline map.
spokenProductionObjective: State transit destinations clearly when requesting assistance.
pragmaticTarget: Navigating regional bus stations and city transit maps.
reviewReason: Synthesize Unit 1 consonant recognition with Unit 2 vowel mastery on geographic names.
audioPurpose: Native pronunciation of compound place names and province designations.
successCriteria: Correctly read 4 Mongolian province names and match with map locations.
Accurately pronounce 'Сүхбаатар' with front vowels throughout the first syllable.
masteryEvidence: Recognizes 'Төв аймаг' on a highway sign instantly.
Distinguishes 'Өвөрхангай' from 'Архангай' in transit route boards.

title: The Seven Short Vowels of Mongolian: А, Э, И, О, У, Ө, Ү
primaryPurpose: Present the complete 7-vowel inventory of Modern Khalkha Cyrillic, establishing their systematic acoustic order.
communicativeOutcome: Recite, write, and visually classify the 7 cardinal short vowels in standard linguistic order.
readingObjective: Read the seven vowel characters in random order across diverse typographic styles.
writingObjective: Transcribe all 7 vowel characters in uppercase and lowercase from memory.
pragmaticTarget: Following literacy curriculum instructions and orthographic classifications.
reviewReason: Integrate Ө and Ү into the comprehensive seven-vowel structural matrix.
audioPurpose: Sequential pure vowel sounds articulated by native speaker.
successCriteria: Correctly write and label the 7 short vowels without omission.
Identify any missing vowel from a scrambled set of 6 characters.
masteryEvidence: Lists the full series А, Э, И, О, У, Ө, Ү without hesitation.
Categorizes each vowel as standard Cyrillic or Mongolian-distinct.

title: Vowel Articulation: Tongue Height, Backness, and Lip Rounding
primaryPurpose: Analyze the articulatory mechanics of open vs mid vs closed and rounded vs unrounded vowels.
communicativeOutcome: Articulate each of the 7 short vowels with accurate tongue position and acoustic clarity.
readingObjective: Associate schematic tongue-position diagrams with the corresponding Cyrillic vowel symbol.
listeningObjective: Discriminate open [a] vs mid [e] vs closed [i] in minimal auditory clips.

spokenProductionObjective: Produce short vowel sounds with crisp onset and termination without diphthongal glide.
pragmaticTarget: Engaging in accurate pronunciation drills with language teachers.
reviewReason: Ground vowel symbols into physical articulatory habits.
audioPurpose: Contrasting acoustic formants of high, mid, and low vowels.
successCriteria: Discriminate high vs low vowel sounds in 8 out of 8 audio tests.
Maintain lip rounding for О, Ө, У, Ү and unrounded spread lips for А, Э, И.
masteryEvidence: No audible glide when pronouncing short [e] or [a].
Clear differentiation between rounded high [u] and unrounded [i].

title: Vowel Resonance in Root Words: Back Roots vs Front Roots
primaryPurpose: Introduce the intuitive concept that words in Mongolian choose either back/masculine or front/feminine vowel sets.
communicativeOutcome: Identify whether simple disyllabic words have back resonance (а/о/у) or front resonance (э/ө/ү).
readingObjective: Classify 10 basic vocabulary items into Back-Vowel words (гал, ус, нар) vs Front-Vowel words (гэр, өдөр, үнэг).
listeningObjective: Detect the holistic acoustic 'timbre' (dark/back vs bright/front) of spoken root words.
writingObjective: Sort written words into two columns on a worksheet based on vowel harmony class.
spokenProductionObjective: Shadow recorded native words preserving unified resonance throughout both syllables.
pragmaticTarget: Developing phonetic intuition for Mongolian word formation.
reviewReason: Prepare foundational intuition for formal vowel harmony rules in Unit 10.
audioPurpose: Authentic resonance contrasts in disyllabic root words.
successCriteria: Sort 10 words into back vs front categories accurately and reliably.
Identify the neutral vowel 'И' appearing comfortably in both classes.
masteryEvidence: Recognizes that 'нар' (sun) and 'гэр' (yurt) belong to opposing vowel harmony classes.
Identifies that words do not mix А and Э in native stems.

title: Decoding Short Vowel Roots: гал, гэр, ус, өвс, нар
primaryPurpose: Build rapid sight-word recognition of elemental natural and domestic monosyllabic nouns.
communicativeOutcome: Read and comprehend foundational monosyllabic words (гал 'fire', гэр 'ger/house', нар 'sun', ус 'water').
readingObjective: Read illustrated environmental flashcards representing core natural elements.
listeningObjective: Match spoken natural nouns with corresponding picture cards.
writingObjective: Write 4 core monosyllabic nouns correctly in Cyrillic.
spokenProductionObjective: Name basic natural elements (sun, water, fire, yurt) when prompted with pictures.
pragmaticTarget: Identifying primary environmental features in rural and urban settings.
reviewReason: Reinforce consonant-vowel blending with cardinal short vowels.
audioPurpose: Clear lexical pronunciation of basic nominal stems.
successCriteria: Read aloud 5 basic nouns with accurate vowel quality.
Spell 'ус', 'гал', 'гэр', 'нар' correctly from audio dictation.
masteryEvidence: Reads 'гэр' with pure short [e] rather than English diphthong.
Matches 'ус' with water and 'гал' with fire immediately.

title: Vowel Discrimination & Acoustic Ear Training: The 7 Vowels
primaryPurpose: Develop acute auditory discrimination of the seven cardinal short vowels across minimal pairs in connected monosyllables and disyllables.
communicativeOutcome: Transcribe any spoken short vowel accurately within monosyllabic and disyllabic words.
readingObjective: Identify intentional vowel spelling errors in a list of 6 simple words.
listeningObjective: Transcribe 10 dictated words focusing on accurate vowel selection.
writingObjective: Write dictated words with 100% accurate vowel representation.
spokenProductionObjective: Read back transcribed words clearly for instructor evaluation.
pragmaticTarget: Completing structured classroom spelling evaluations.
reviewReason: Unit 3 synthesis checkpoint consolidating cardinal vowel literacy.
audioPurpose: Standardized diagnostic audio dictation items.
successCriteria: Achieve accurately and reliably on vowel dictation assessment.
Zero confusion between back and front vowel counterparts.
masteryEvidence: Spells 'толгой', 'дэвтэр', 'улс', 'хүүхэд' with correct short vowels in root positions.
Identifies that 'хэн' contains vowel Э and 'хүн' contains Ү.

title: Obstruents of Mongolian: Б, П, Д, Т, Г, Ц, Ч, З, Ж
primaryPurpose: Introduce the full inventory of Mongolian plosives, affricates, and their written Cyrillic letterforms.
communicativeOutcome: Recognize, name, and transcribe the 9 obstruent consonant characters in printed and written forms.
readingObjective: Read isolated consonants Б, П, Д, Т, Г, Ц, Ч, З, Ж across varied typefaces.
writingObjective: Write the glyphs Ц, Ч, З, Ж, Д with correct stroke order and distinguishing descenders.
pragmaticTarget: Following alphabetical classroom chart prompts.
reviewReason: Expand initial consonant set into the full obstruent series.
audioPurpose: Clear phonetic demonstration of non-aspirated vs aspirated stops.
successCriteria: Distinguish visually between similar glyphs (Ц vs Щ, Ч vs У, З vs Э).
Write all 9 obstruent consonants without visual errors.
masteryEvidence: Does not confuse Ц with Russian Щ.
Identifies that Ч has an open upper-left bowl compared to У.

title: Aspiration Contrast: Fortis (п, т, к, ц, ч) vs Lenis (б, д, г, з, ж)
primaryPurpose: Train auditory discrimination and articulatory production of the aspiration contrast characterizing Mongolian obstruents.
communicativeOutcome: Pronounce and differentiate aspirated voiceless stops from unaspirated lax stops without voicing confusion.
readingObjective: Read minimal stop pairs: бар (tiger) vs пар (steam), дас (accustom) vs тас (vulture).
listeningObjective: Identify whether an initial stop is aspirated (fortis) or unaspirated (lenis) in native audio.
writingObjective: Write the correct initial consonant letter based on auditory aspiration cues.
spokenProductionObjective: Produce strong aspiration on Т and П while keeping Д and Б completely unaspirated.
pragmaticTarget: Achieving phonemic accuracy in everyday speech.
reviewReason: Acoustically ground the written obstruent letterforms.
audioPurpose: Precise recording of aspiration burst dynamics in initial stops.
successCriteria: Score 8/10 on an auditory stop-voicing/aspiration discrimination task.
Demonstrate physical aspiration difference using paper-deflection test.
masteryEvidence: Articulates 'та' without voicing and with crisp post-release aspiration.
Articulates 'да' as a voiceless lax lenis stop without English-style voiced lead.

title: Sonorant Consonants: М, Н, Л, Р, В, Й
primaryPurpose: Introduce the sonorant series (nasals, lateral, trill, and approximants) and their positional phonotactics.
communicativeOutcome: Read and pronounce sonorant consonants in initial, medial, and coda positions with natural resonance.
readingObjective: Read words with complex sonorant codas (мал, зам, үнэн, нар, сар).
listeningObjective: Recognize word-final velar nasal /ŋ/ (written as н) vs alveolar /n/ in spoken Mongolian.
writingObjective: Write 5 sonorant-rich nouns from oral dictation.
spokenProductionObjective: Produce the alveolar trill Р (/r/) in word-final position without American-style retroflex coloring.
pragmaticTarget: Reading domestic livestock and geographic terminology.
reviewReason: Complete the inventory of consonants in combination with short vowels.
audioPurpose: Authentic Khalkha lateral and velar nasal articulation.
successCriteria: Correctly articulate final -л and -р in words like 'сар' (moon) and 'мал' (livestock).
Spell dictated sonorant coda words without errors.
masteryEvidence: Distinguishes between alveolar 'н' and velar 'н' [ŋ] at the end of words.
Reads 'зам' (road) with clear bilabial closure.

title: Decoding Street Signs & Basic Nominal Stems: гудамж, зам, буудал
primaryPurpose: Decode authentic public transit and municipal signs combining newly learned obstruents and sonorants.
communicativeOutcome: Read and understand street signs (гудамж 'street', зам 'road', буудал 'station/stop', цагдаа 'police').

reviewReason: Apply full consonant inventory to urban civic signage.

successCriteria: Match 5 authentic street/transit signs with their English meanings.
Accurately pronounce 'гудамж' with proper affricate Ж ending.
masteryEvidence: Instantly decodes 'Автобусны буудал' on a bus shelter.
Identifies 'Цагдаа' on an emergency police station sign.

title: Consonant Inventory Synthesis & Dictation Checkpoint
primaryPurpose: Consolidate consonant grapheme-phoneme correspondences through systematic auditory dictation and spelling evaluation.
communicativeOutcome: Spell, read, and discriminate any standard Mongolian consonant sound in root-initial and root-final positions.

audioPurpose: Standardized phonetic assessment recording of consonant stems.
successCriteria: Score accurately and reliably on consonant spelling dictation.
Demonstrate zero confusion between Д and Т, or Б and П in dictation.
masteryEvidence: Correctly spells 'буудал', 'цаг', 'зам', 'өдөр', 'нөхөр' upon hearing native audio.
Accurately articulates all stops during oral reading verification.

title: Mongolian Cyrillic Keyboard Layout & The Home Row
primaryPurpose: Introduce the standard Mongolian Cyrillic keyboard layout (MN QWERTY) and key positions on the home row.
communicativeOutcome: Locate and type home-row characters (ф, ц, у, в, а, п, р, о, л, д, ж, э) on a standard keyboard without visual hunting.

writingObjective: Type home-row consonant-vowel combinations with accurate finger placement.

Identify the key locations for А, О, Л, and Д without looking at key labels.
masteryEvidence: Operates Mongolian keyboard layout without reverting to system Latin defaults.
Types disyllabic home-row syllables fluently.

title: Locating Mongolian Specific Keys: Ө and Ү
primaryPurpose: Train muscle memory for typing the Mongolian-specific keys Ө and Ү, typically mapped to =/+ and -/_ or bracket keys.

Input both lowercase (ө, ү) and uppercase (Ө, Ү) forms using Shift correctly.

Does not mistakenly type О instead of Ө when typing under time constraints.

title: Typing Search Queries, Names, and Map Destinations

Input destination names without autocorrect interference.

Searches for 'төв шуудан' (Central Post Office) with correct vowel spelling.

title: Digital Composition Workshop: Typing Personal Names & Search Queries
primaryPurpose: Apply keyboard touch-typing skills to practical digital tasks: composing short name searches, contact notes, and digital messaging.

Successfully input digits and punctuation symbols commonly used in Mongolian.

Corrects mistyped characters using backspace instinctively.

title: Counting from Zero to Five: тэг, нэг, хоёр, гурав, дөрөв, таван

title: Counting from Six to Ten: зургаа, долоо, найм, ес, арав

Count forward from 1 to 10 and backward from 10 to 1 fluently.

Recognizes 'найм' and 'ес' without confusing initial iotated Е.

Differentiate between 'уншаарай' (please read) and 'бичээрэй' (please write).

Listens quietly upon hearing 'Сонсоорой'.

primaryPurpose: Provide the learner with vital survival phrases to request repetition or signal comprehension in class.
